config.title: List Virtualization

intro.title: List Virtualization
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a virtualized list component that efficiently displays a large dataset by only rendering the items currently visible in the viewport. You'll learn the core concept of list virtualization, which dramatically improves performance by reducing DOM elements and memory usage. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript for logic, and CSS for styling the scrollable container. By the end, you'll understand how to implement a basic virtual scrolling mechanism that loads items on-demand as the user scrolls.
intro.usecase: List virtualization is essential in Angular applications that handle large datasets, such as data tables in financial dashboards displaying thousands of transactions or social media feeds showing endless posts. Product teams use this technique to maintain smooth scrolling performance in e-commerce category pages with hundreds of products or in admin panels showing extensive user lists. Without virtualization, these interfaces would become sluggish and consume excessive memory, directly impacting user experience. As an Angular developer, implementing virtual scrolling ensures your data-heavy components remain responsive while handling real-world scale.

objectives: Implement a virtual scrolling directive to optimize list rendering
Configure the CDK virtual scroll viewport with appropriate item size
Bind a large dataset to a virtual scroll viewport component
Manipulate the scroll position to test virtualization behavior
Initialize a virtual scrolling strategy for dynamic content
Construct a reusable virtual list component with Angular templates
Apply performance monitoring to compare virtualized vs non-virtualized lists

steps.title: Import Angular modules and components
steps.instruction: Import Component, OnInit, and CdkVirtualScrollViewport from their respective Angular modules.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in these Angular core and CDK modules. Component and OnInit come from '@angular/core', while CdkVirtualScrollViewport comes from '@angular/cdk/scrolling'.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component, OnInit, and CdkVirtualScrollViewport here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular modules for list virtualization are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Component and OnInit are imported from '@angular/core', and CdkVirtualScrollViewport is imported from '@angular/cdk/scrolling'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've imported all three items: Component, OnInit, and CdkVirtualScrollViewport from their correct module paths.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Remember to import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and CdkVirtualScrollViewport from '@angular/cdk/scrolling'.

steps.title: Create the main component class
steps.instruction: Create a component class named 'VirtualListComponent' with the @Component decorator and implement OnInit.
steps.hint: Use the imported Component and OnInit to define your class. The class should have the correct name and implement the interface.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';

// Create the VirtualListComponent class here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a properly defined Angular component class ready for implementing list virtualization.
successCriteria: The VirtualListComponent class is created with @Component decorator and implements OnInit.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both the @Component decorator and implement OnInit in your class definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Check that you're using the correct class name, decorator, and interface implementation.

steps.title: Initialize sample data array
steps.instruction: Inside the VirtualListComponent class, define a property called 'items' and initialize it as an array of objects with 'id' and 'content' properties.
steps.hint: You can create a property in the class and assign it an array of objects. Each object should have numeric 'id' and string 'content' fields.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a sample data array ready for the virtualized list to display.
successCriteria: The 'items' property is defined as an array of objects, each with 'id' and 'content' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined an array, but make sure each object has both 'id' and 'content' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The items array isn't properly defined. It should be an array of objects with 'id' and 'content' properties.

steps.title: Configure virtual scroll viewport
steps.instruction: Add a property named 'itemSize' with a value of 50 and a property named 'viewportHeight' with a value of '400px' to your component class.
steps.hint: Add two properties in the component class: itemSize: number = 50; and viewportHeight: string = '400px';
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component class will have two new properties that will be used for virtual scroll configuration.
successCriteria: The component class contains both 'itemSize: number = 50;' and 'viewportHeight: string = '400px';' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added one of the properties, but both 'itemSize' and 'viewportHeight' are needed for virtual scroll configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class doesn't contain the required properties. Add 'itemSize: number = 50;' and 'viewportHeight: string = '400px';' to configure the virtual scroll viewport.

steps.title: Add template structure with virtual scroll
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add the cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport element with the required attributes for virtualization.
steps.hint: Add the viewport element inside the template property of the @Component decorator. Use the itemSize attribute to define the height of each item.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: basic virtual scroll viewport
<cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport itemSize="50">
  <!-- Items will go here -->
</cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains a cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport element ready for virtualized content.
successCriteria: The template property contains a cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport element with the itemSize attribute set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the viewport element, but make sure it has the required itemSize attribute for proper virtualization.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template still needs the cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport element. Check that you've added it inside the template property.

steps.title: Configure virtual scroll properties
steps.instruction: Add itemSize, minBufferPx, and maxBufferPx properties to the virtual scroll element in your template.
steps.hint: These properties control the size of each item and the buffer zones for smoother scrolling.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: configuring virtual scroll properties -->
<cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport itemSize="50" minBufferPx="100" maxBufferPx="200">
  <!-- content -->
</cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport>
steps.expectedOutcome: The virtual scroll element will have itemSize, minBufferPx, and maxBufferPx properties configured.
successCriteria: The template includes itemSize, minBufferPx, and maxBufferPx properties on the virtual scroll element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added all three properties: itemSize, minBufferPx, and maxBufferPx.
steps.feedbackWrong: The virtual scroll properties are not configured correctly. Check the example and try again.

steps.title: Add list items with ngFor
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add the *cdkVirtualFor directive to the <div> element to iterate through the items array and display each item's name.
steps.hint: Use the syntax *cdkVirtualFor="let item of items" and display {{ item.name }} inside the div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The virtual scroll viewport will now have a directive that iterates through the items array and displays each item's name.
successCriteria: The <div> element inside the viewport has the *cdkVirtualFor directive with proper syntax to iterate through the items array and display item.name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check the syntax. Make sure you're using *cdkVirtualFor="let item of items" and displaying {{ item.name }} inside the div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The *cdkVirtualFor directive is missing or has incorrect syntax. Remember to use *cdkVirtualFor="let item of items" to iterate through the items array and display each item's name.

steps.title: Style the list container
steps.instruction: Add a CSS class to the viewport container and define its styles in the component's styleUrls array.
steps.hint: You need to create a CSS file and link it to the component. Start by adding a class name to the viewport element and then create the corresponding CSS file with the viewport styles.
steps.expectedOutcome: The viewport container will have a CSS class applied and the component will reference a CSS file for styling.
successCriteria: The viewport element has a class attribute and the styleUrls array includes a CSS file path.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both the class attribute and styleUrls array are properly configured.
steps.feedbackWrong: The viewport container needs a CSS class and the component needs to reference a CSS file. Check the analogous example for guidance.

steps.title: Add scroll event handler
steps.instruction: In the VirtualListComponent class, create a method named handleScroll that takes an Event parameter and logs the scroll position to the console.
steps.hint: Add a method inside the component class that logs the scrollTop property from the event target.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a handleScroll method that logs scroll events, preparing for scroll tracking in virtualization.
successCriteria: A handleScroll method with Event parameter is added to the component class and logs scroll position.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it takes an Event parameter and logs the scroll position.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleScroll method is missing or doesn't match the requirements.

steps.title: Wire scroll event to viewport
steps.instruction: In the template, add the (scrolledIndexChange) event binding to the cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport element to call your handleScroll method.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (scrolledIndexChange)="handleScroll($event)". This connects the virtual scroll's index change event to your handler.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: binding a click event -->
<button (click)="handleClick($event)">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport element now has an event binding that will trigger the handleScroll method when the scroll index changes.
successCriteria: The cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport element includes (scrolledIndexChange)="handleScroll($event)" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the (scrolledIndexChange) event binding with the correct syntax: (scrolledIndexChange)="handleScroll($event)".
steps.feedbackWrong: The scroll event isn't properly connected. Check that you've added the (scrolledIndexChange) event binding to the cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport element with the correct syntax.

steps.title: Add loading indicator for buffer
steps.instruction: Add a boolean property 'isLoading' to your component class and initialize it to false.
steps.hint: Declare a property with type boolean and set its initial value in the class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has a boolean property 'isLoading' initialized to false, which will control the loading indicator visibility.
successCriteria: The component class contains a property named 'isLoading' of type boolean with initial value false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared a property named 'isLoading' with type boolean and initialized it to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class should have a boolean property named 'isLoading' initialized to false. Check the property declaration syntax.

steps.title: Test virtualization with large dataset
steps.instruction: Expand the items array to include 1000 sample items to test the virtual scroll performance.
steps.hint: Use a loop or array spread to generate a larger dataset while keeping the same item structure.
steps.analogousExample:
// Expanding an array with a loop
items = Array.from({ length: 1000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, name: `Item ${i + 1}` }));
steps.expectedOutcome: The items array should contain 1000 objects with sequential IDs and names, enabling you to observe smooth scrolling performance through the virtualized list.
successCriteria: The items array is expanded to 1000 elements while maintaining the correct structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've expanded the array, but make sure it contains exactly 1000 items with sequential IDs and names like 'Item 1', 'Item 2', etc.
steps.feedbackWrong: The items array still contains only a few items. Use Array.from or a loop to generate 1000 items for proper virtualization testing.
